2610.06673.title: The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance
2610.06673.paper_summary: Are language models compliant with user instructions? A model that always complies can be stopped but also exploited, while one that always resists can be neither exploited nor stopped. We contribute an open two-probe benchmark that can place any language model on this spectrum. In the active probe, a user instructs the model to act and accept a lower payoff, which measures exploitability. In the passive probe, the user instructs it to wait and give up a higher payoff, which measures stoppability. The two compliance rates combine into a compliance index $κ$. Applied to twelve language models, the benchmark shows that seven mostly follow the instruction in both probes and justify their action by pointing to the instruction. Only Claude Sonnet-4.6 and Claude Opus-4.7 can be stopped without being exploitable, Claude Opus-4.6 and GPT-5-mini resist both instructions, and no model is exploitable but unstoppable. Knowing where a language model sits on the compliance index $κ$ matters for human operators and for multi-agent systems, whether distributed or orchestrated.
2610.06673.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型是否遵循用戶指示？一個始終遵從的模型可以被停止，但也可能被利用，而一個始終抵抗的模型則無法被利用或停止。我們貢獻了一個開放的雙探針基準，可以將任何語言模型放置在這個範疇中。在主動探針中，用戶指示模型行動並接受較低的報酬，這測量了可利用性。在被動探針中，用戶指示它等待並放棄較高的報酬，這測量了可停止性。這兩個遵從率結合成一個遵從指數 $κ$。應用於十二個語言模型，基準顯示七個模型在兩個探針中大多遵循指示，並通過指向指示來證明其行動的合理性。只有 Claude Sonnet-4.6 和 Claude Opus-4.7 可以在不被利用的情況下被停止，Claude Opus-4.6 和 GPT-5-mini 則抵抗兩個指示，且沒有模型是可利用但無法停止的。了解一個語言模型在遵從指數 $κ$ 上的位置對於人類操作員和多代理系統（無論是分散式還是協調式）都很重要。
